conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A is the only output a keyboard user can actually operate: its rollback confirmation traps focus, closes on Escape, and survives the freshness tick, all reproduced locally, while B rebuilds the entire DOM every second, wiping focus app-wide including inside its open confirmation dialog, whose Escape and Tab containment do not work. B has the stronger five-second priority signal (the ACT NOW hero) and shows capacity data by default where A hides it behind a retry, but A's flaw is recoverable in one labeled click while B's failures block safe completion of the job's riskiest action. A also handles state semantics more honestly (real stale-clock behavior, disclosed time-range meaning, no test scaffolding in the product UI).
suspected_unblinding: none — the two builds use different visual languages (light utilitarian vs dark ops theme) but nothing identifies a treatment or builder

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: Rollback dialog asserts 'Reversible: a subsequent deploy can restore 2026.07.28.3' — a capability not supplied by the brief, and it makes the destructive action read as safer than the facts support (minor but decision-adjacent).

findings.label: A
findings.description: Decision-driving capacity facts (checkout workers 94% utilization, 12 minutes of queue runway) are hidden by default behind the capacity-failure state and appear only after clicking Retry, so the urgency signal is absent from the initial view and from every packet capture.
findings.evidence: source/app.js state.capacityFailed=true at boot; reproduced locally — default zone C shows only the failure message, and after Retry it renders '94% / 12 min queue capacity left'

findings.label: A
findings.description: Closing the rollback dialog does not return focus to the triggering button — render() replaces the node before .focus() is called on the stale reference, so focus falls to the document body.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally: after Escape, document.activeElement is the page body, not 'Roll back payments-api'; source/app.js closeRollbackModal() renders before focusing lastFocusedTrigger

findings.label: A
findings.description: The rollback dialog gives initial focus to the destructive 'Confirm rollback' button, so Enter pressed immediately after opening executes the rollback.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally: document.activeElement is 'Confirm rollback' on open; source/app.js render() focuses .btn--modal-confirm

findings.label: A
findings.description: Search is badged 'Elevated' (yellow) although its 0.9% error rate breaches the 0.5% SLO; the displayed values and targets mitigate but the label understates the state B correctly badges as an error-SLO breach.

findings.label: B
findings.description: A timer rebuilds the entire app via innerHTML every 1000 ms, destroying keyboard focus everywhere — including inside the open rollback confirmation dialog — so a keyboard-only operator cannot reliably complete or cancel the console's riskiest action.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally: focus set on a button falls to body within 2 s, and focus placed on the dialog's Cancel button is lost after one tick; source/app.js clockTimer calls render() every 1000 ms

findings.label: B
findings.description: The rollback dialog declares aria-modal but implements none of the modal contract: no initial focus, no focus trap (Tab moves into the background page), and Escape does not close it; the runbook drawer behaves the same.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally: modal remains open after Escape, and Tab from 'Confirm rollback' lands outside the dialog (closest('.modal') null); no keydown handler exists in source/app.js

findings.label: B
findings.description: The root container carries aria-live="polite" while the whole tree is re-rendered every second, which would cause screen readers to re-announce dashboard content continuously.
findings.evidence: source/index.html <main id="app" aria-live="polite"> combined with the 1 s full render loop in source/app.js

findings.label: B
findings.description: Changing the time range changes nothing except the button's own pressed state — no label, window annotation, or data context updates — so the required interaction is only nominally satisfied and the control's meaning is undefined.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally: header text identical before and after selecting 24h; evidence/interaction-03-change-time-range.png shows no visible change beyond the pressed button

findings.label: B
findings.description: The Image processing card asserts a 'WITHIN SLO' badge while simultaneously stating its metrics could not be loaded, asserting a status for which the UI claims to have no data.
findings.evidence: reproduced locally and visible in every B capture, e.g. evidence/state-02-partial-data-failure.png

findings.label: B
findings.description: Demo scaffolding ('Test controls: Force stale-data notice / Reset image processing failure') is rendered inside the product UI in every capture, and the forced stale banner contradicts itself ('last updated 0s ago' while claiming staleness begins at 120s).
